per_item.argument: The source treats a spatially homogeneous but anisotropic Bianchi I metric. The local datum makes its torus, regularity, units and directional rates explicit.
The source’s Bianchi I component equations provide a cross-check; the complete local Christoffel, Riemann and Ricci calculation is supplied on the A page.

The source derives the Kasner constraints through an invariant-basis ODE and generic eigenvalue diagonalization. The local proof instead substitutes exact Ricci components and includes repeated exponents and the static case.
The source lists the representative exponent triple; the example proves anisotropy, shear scaling and nonflatness directly.
The source identifies the exceptional flat triple and gives a Milne coordinate map. The local example proves the map only on a coordinate lift and makes no global torus identification.

contents.name: Diagonal Bianchi I specialization and vacuum Einstein component equations, equations (159)–(162)
contents.support: Independent cross-check for the diagonal homogeneous ansatz and component calculation. The local lemma derives every coefficient with c retained and extends it to the specified C2 quotient metric.

contents.support: The source’s smooth coordinate convention is a sign/order cross-check only. C2 regularity, connection uniqueness and quotient-atlas patching are separately proved in the local definition.

contents.name: Kasner derivation and exponent constraints, equations (163)–(172)
contents.support: Independent treatment of the nonstatic power-law branch. Its route uses invariant-basis ODEs and generic eigenvalue diagonalization; the local Ricci-component proof covers all exponent multiplicities and the static case without that restriction.

contents.support: Cross-check for the flat exceptional branch. The local example proves curvature vanishes and supplies its own invertible coordinate map in a local lift; no global torus coordinate transformation is inferred.

contents.support: Cross-check for the selected exact exponent triple; anisotropy and nonzero curvature are established by local calculations.

contents.name: Bianchi IX Kasner transitions and Mixmaster dynamics, Section 4.3.2 and later sections
contents.reason: The assigned pair proves neither generic BKL oscillations nor a statement about arbitrary anisotropic or inhomogeneous developments.

sources.reading_note: The notes use signature (-,+,+,+), natural units c=G=1 and a homogeneous invariant basis. The author’s diagonalization discussion treats generic distinct eigenvalues before listing special triples. No c=1 formula, generic diagonalization assumption, Bianchi IX transition or singularity claim is imported; the local proof uses explicit component formulas with SI c and covers repeated/static cases.
